title: Codex plugin dogfood scenario manifest
description: Scenario definitions for the real-Codex dogfood. parle owns bring-up, credentials, driving, and the verdict; it judges `authoritative` checks from its database and wire evidence. The `diagnostic` checks are judged from the Codex rollout JSONL by packages/codex-plugin/dogfood/rollout.mjs.

placeholders.description: Every `{{token}}` the harness substitutes in `task` and check strings before use. Any placeholder used in the manifest must be listed here.

adaptersIssue.description: parlehq/parle-adapters issue number this scenario verifies.

driver.description: exec: one `codex exec` turn. app-server: a persistent thread driven over the Codex app-server protocol so hooks can wake an idle turn.

catalog.description: How the harness seeds ~/.parle/profiles. two-profile: [default] holds the peer identity and [codex] holds the expected identity. default-only: only [default] exists, so PARLE_PROFILE=codex resolves nothing.

env.description: Launch-shell environment the harness exports before starting Codex. Names must appear in the plugin .mcp.json env_vars list, or Codex's cleared MCP environment drops them.

capMinutes.description: Wall-clock cap for the turn; only attended-hold uses it.

authoritativeCheck.description: Judged by parle from room state. participant-identity: the live participant belongs to the seeded identity and the room. authored-probe: the expected participant authored a message containing bodyContains. beacon-echo: an authored reply contains {{beacon}}. cursor-advanced: responsive_delivery_cursor.last_acked_seq >= the ask seq. no-authored-messages: zero messages authored during the scenario window by the named seeded identity, or with agent `any` by every seeded identity's session, so a fallback to the wrong identity still fails. The scenario window runs from container start to teardown.

diagnosticCheck.description: Judged from the Codex rollout JSONL. tool-calls: count of calls to `tool` within [min, max], optionally only counting calls whose arguments contain argsSubset; fails if any counted call has an argument matching argsForbid (numeric `gt` / `eq` predicates per argument name). no-shell-polling: no shell command with a loop or sleep in command position (while, until, for … in, sleep, watch) that also performs a Parle network or inbox operation (curl/wget/http to a parle host or /v/ path, or a parle_inbox/parle_read invocation). status-text: applied to the text returned by parle_status tool results. agent-message: applied to the final assistant message (contains = all, containsAny = at least one). hook-delivery-present: a developer or user message carries 'Parle responsive delivery seq='.
